title: Replayable procedural-opponent single-rollout smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Per-hand seeded procedural opponent styles can create an auditable non-learned opponent distribution while preserving correctly sampled PPO hero behavior and exact physical-hand accounting; a short smoke should show diverse style/action coverage, no opponent inference requests, deterministic replay, and finite optimization metrics.
material_change: Add a single-rollout-only, fixed-seed per-hand procedural opponent contract with independent RNG, broad fold/call/raise style parameters, separate evidence metrics, and incompatibility guards for adaptive league and multi-rollout. Run unit/contract tests and a short learned-weight smoke only; no Slumbot evaluation.
baseline: Current v6 sampled-PPO trainer with fixed learned opponents and no procedural opponent path.

notes: Preregistered as a contract and very-short smoke before implementation. Procedural opponents are general environment-side action policies, not benchmark-specific rules; heldout style evaluation is deferred until this contract passes.
Six contract tests passed before launch, including a real 50-hand worker/shared-memory test with only HERO_MODEL_ID inference requests.

r1 preserved intact: it found that pipe-only procedural metrics omitted JSONL and 86 shutdown-tail hands. Added shared cumulative procedural accounting, JSONL/checkpoint/manifest persistence, and 25 relevant passing tests before r2.

r1 completed 4,486 physical hands but exposed an evidence defect: pipe-only procedural metrics were absent from JSONL and omitted 86 shutdown-tail hands. r1 artifacts remain immutable and were not used as the passing result.
r2 shared accounting is authoritative and includes all completed worker tails. Training reward versus the procedural population is not external-strength evidence and was not used for promotion.

result.summary: Implemented and verified replayable per-hand procedural opponent domain randomization. Corrected r2 completed 4,463 physical training hands and 16,730 procedural decisions; exact shared accounting, checkpoint/manifest/JSONL agreement, deterministic 8-profile replay, all 9 action-slot coverage, finite PPO metrics, and 25 relevant tests all passed.
result.conclusion: The single-rollout procedural-opponent mechanism is technically valid, replayable, checkpoint-safe, and fast enough for a small learned-weight experiment. This smoke establishes only the data-generation contract, not poker strength; no Slumbot hands were used.
result.next_step: Run one small matched control-versus-procedural training pilot from the exact raw parent, evaluate both frozen endpoints on untouched heldout procedural style seeds and the existing parent-state preservation corpus, and require a clear matched advantage plus acceptable preservation before any Slumbot allocation.
